pull_request.title: Calorimeter: propose LAr side-neck routing and gap mitigation
pull_request.head: codex/lar-gap-hadron-options
pull_request.body:
This draft proposes barrel outer-side necks that complete outward service offsets before the barrel end, a straight exterior axial bus, and radial extraction through the rear service break. It addresses the weak LAr barrel/endcap handover seen in the matched10k study, while retaining unresolved engineering interfaces.

RZ views now show the old/new routes at identical detector positions, plus a separate conditional400mm front-gap view. The figures use fixed ECAL/HCAL colours, physical-width100mm jackets and20mm clearance offsets; the500mm full radial exit stays explicit despite900mm behind the conditionally shifted endcap. PNG/SVG exports, pinned source/script/output hashes and reproduction recipe: [drawing README](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/lar-gap-hadron-options/docs/design/inputs/lar-gap-options/routing-rz/README.md).

The proposed one-metre neck band, R3029 bus and R4800 handoff are screening reservations. Existing pipes,4xOD bends, station/channel counts and planning capacity are retained initially. The100mm utility offset has a739.403mm legacy envelope; the ideal rear turn requires490mm with both face clearances, leaving only10mm in the500mm break. Ports, support/board repacking, complete bundles, external handoff and the forward collar remain engineering gates. No geometry export or reduced-gap fit is established.

Selective layer/region coarsening remains a separate option. Channel reduction alone leaves the existing cryogenic bend unchanged, and lossless regrouping preserves the10k all-cell energy sum. This does not establish calibrated hadron-collider superiority.

Validation: bounded SysArch/PhysVal contributions; corrected final RZ visual/source review; all4PNG/SVG exports and receipt reproduce byte-identically; XML, source/output hashes, analytical band/bend/gap bounds and pinned-input guard checks pass. Three original service controls and project/session/inventory checks are retained. No native route/material/shower or structural/thermal qualification was performed. Current-head CI is separate; prior green checks are not inferred to cover later commits.

Related: PR75 transition review; merged PR138/139 placement work and PR14010k comparison. Selected prompts, source/role/work labels and available exact disjoint token logs are retained. Draft only; no readiness, merge or human design acceptance inferred.

**Yes—selectively larger readout cells could reduce services, but changing the service routing is the more direct route to a smaller gap.**

For a hadron collider, I would preserve fine front/strip layers and test coarser readout deeper in the calorimeter. Doubling both transverse cell dimensions could give roughly four times fewer channels. However, pileup, nearby showers and track–cluster matching still demand fine segmentation; hadron operation does not automatically favour larger cells. [FCC-hh calorimeter study](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.09962)

The current budget illustrates the distinction: halving channels halves the assumed channel-proportional electronics power, but leaves the **739 mm cryogenic pipe-bend envelope unchanged**. The **800 mm warm barrel–endcap gap is a routing hypothesis**, not an established LAr minimum.

I would prioritize:

1. **Side/rear service exits:** remove the front pipe bend as the gap-setting constraint.
2. **Better active coverage:** investigate an inward endcap shift together with a barrel extension or shaped overlap. These require revised cryostat and forward-region interfaces.
3. **Less passive corner material:** revisit closures, supports and electronics placement.
4. **Instrument the remaining crack:** a presampler or gap detector could improve corrections, although it cannot replace missing shower depth.

Cell regrouping alone also leaves our existing all-cell energy sum unchanged. Choosing granularity therefore needs clustering, noise, pileup and shower-separation studies. The 10k result makes LAr promising, but does not yet establish superior hadron-collider performance.

events.text:
**GAP-HADRON-PhysVal — `ce9c261a94aa2b025180f2f5c96d5e166fa01a53`**

Layer- and region-dependent readout coarsening is a reasonable **prototype hypothesis**, but the existing 10k study cannot select its granularity or qualify hadron-collider performance.

**What the response study establishes**

The represented LAr candidate has smaller inclusive raw-response width than staggered Si–W: **17.84% versus 39.27%**. In the transition, however, widths are **44.18% versus 47.21%**. The transition width difference has paired 95% interval **−0.75 to +7.05 percentage points**, so no transition-region advantage is established. These are spectrum-averaged active-deposit widths without noise, collection response, digitization or pileup. Sources: pinned `docs/validation/lar10k/README.md:9–34,40–49` and `summary.json`, `width_contrasts.siw_staggered_minus_lar.broad_eta`.

I additionally inspected the bound retained LAr ledger: **all 183 events below half the inclusive mean occur in 1.2≤|eta|<1.5**, with observed |eta| **1.30849–1.37137**. This is descriptive localization, not evidence that a particular pipe or gap component caused the losses. Ledger SHA256 matches the pinned summary: `de5cc13cc53436b3422c59a23af72d21bd8a631e976aa752aec09d8d500bd750`.

The service review already states that **800 mm is the chosen routing allowance, not an intrinsic LAr minimum**. Actual port origins and connected routes remain undefined. Sources: `docs/design/inputs/DES-032-transition-review.md:12–42`; DES033’s transition discussion.

**The essential coarsening distinction**

The current observable is \(R=\sum_i E_i/E_{\rm primary}\). For any lossless partition into larger cells,

\[
\sum_{\text{groups}}\sum_{i\in\text{group}}E_i=\sum_iE_i.
\]

Consequently, regrouping cells or longitudinal compartments preserves the current raw-response curve. Existing 10k energy-sum results therefore provide **no granularity optimization criterion**.

Keep the physical absorber/electrode sampling pitch fixed in the first regrouping study. Changing the 1536 physical barrel periods, absorber thickness or liquid gaps changes shower sampling and requires a separate geometry/physics comparison. DES032 distinguishes its physical periods from two-electrode readout grouping and the theta grid (`:78–103`); DES033 distinguishes physical wheels from virtual radial/axial cells (`:10–21,35–40`).

A useful hypothesis is to preserve fine early/shower-discrimination information while testing coarser rear readout. Region-dependent choices should follow reconstructed angular separation, occupancy and pileup requirements; the poorly responding transition should not automatically receive coarser segmentation.

**Hadron-collider implications**

- Larger logical cells can degrade shower separation, electron/photon and tau identification, pointing, pileup rejection and track–cluster association. Higher occupancy is not an argument by itself for coarsening the forward region.
- Hardware ganging changes input capacitance and noise correlations. Summing already digitized fine channels does not model one larger electrode feeding fewer frontends. ALLEGRO explicitly studies the granularity–capacitance/noise–crosstalk tradeoff. [ALLEGRO proceedings, §3/PDF4]([external URL redacted; see source journal]).
- Hadron-collider precedent supports retaining useful lateral and longitudinal information: ATLAS increased trigger granularity to improve shower discrimination and pileup handling. This is context, not a prescription for nODD cell dimensions. [ATLAS Phase-I LAr readout paper, §§1–2](https://arxiv.org/html/2202.07384v2).
- Reduced frontend power or material requires an actual changed board/ASIC inventory. Post-processing aggregation alone reduces neither installed frontend count nor the current cold-service geometry.
- Channel count alone does not determine bandwidth: hit rate, occupancy, waveform samples and aggregation overhead also change. The current 50 kHz/channel scenario is expressly a planning hypothesis.

**Discriminating validation**

1. Define the intended bunch spacing/pileup envelope, object momentum range, angular separation goals, timing/dynamic-range requirements and reconstruction scope; do not import numerical requirements from ATLAS or FCC-ee.
2. Perform reversible grouping studies on existing fine hits, checking exact energy conservation and channel maps. Evaluate position/shower-shape information and two-shower separation, not inclusive energy sums alone.
3. Add capacitance-dependent electronics/noise, correlated noise, thresholds and in-/out-of-time pileup before estimating actual reconstruction or resource tradeoffs.
4. Investigate transition geometry separately through service-complete routing alternatives, native material/active-depth scans and targeted fixed-energy showers across both eta signs and several phi phases. Preserve the unchanged baseline and use fresh validation events.

**Actual checks**

Read all pinned inputs; inspected the preserved summary/covariance and bound ledger; reran the pinned service arithmetic in memory. A labelled **half-channel planning test** halves assumed electronics power **86/172/258→43/86/129 kW**, while the **100 mm utility-line S-bend remains 739.403 mm**. Thus coarsening alone does not demonstrate a smaller front service gap.

No files changed, native runtime activated, simulation launched or design accepted. The ATLAS paper is a new supporting source if the coordinator cites it in the design note; the ALLEGRO proceedings already have catalogue ID `SRC-ALLEGRO-EPS-2025`.

events.text:
`GAP-HADRON-SysArch` — reviewed **ce9c261a94aa2b025180f2f5c96d5e166fa01a53**, read-only under the explicitly supplied SysArch mandate.

The first useful mitigation study is **real service routing plus coupled barrel/endcap geometry**. Channel coarsening alone does not shorten the present front gap.

- **Current gap driver:** the 800 mm warm-vessel gap is a prototype topology choice. The assumed 100 mm utility jacket, bend radius 4×OD, 293.7 mm radial displacement and 20 mm clearance reproduce a **739.403 mm** S-bend envelope. Actual utility origins, ports and connections remain undefined; this is not an established LAr minimum. [Transition review, lines19–39](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/ce9c261a94aa2b025180f2f5c96d5e166fa01a53/docs/design/inputs/DES-032-transition-review.md#L19-L39)

- **Coarsening:** it can reduce aggregation, electronics, bandwidth and heat requirements, but current bend arithmetic depends only on pipe dimensions and endpoints. Recalculation gives barrel cable packed area **3,516.62 mm²**, versus **27,587.11 mm²** ordinary pipe allowance and **78,539.82 mm²** additional utility allowance. Even removing every cable would leave the assumed limiting bend unchanged. Smaller cooling lines would require a new thermal/hydraulic assessment; utility fill/vent/relief dimensions cannot simply scale with channel count. [services.py, lines15–65](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/ce9c261a94aa2b025180f2f5c96d5e166fa01a53/tools/lar_calorimeter/services.py#L15-L65)

- **Side/rear egress:** worth screening first, with named ports and connected routes. The selected exterior corridor is 300 mm beside the barrel but only 181 mm beside the endcap; the rear allocation is already 500 mm. Rear readout routing additionally encounters the **continuous, unported 30 mm support annulus**, which presently blocks electrode-to-board signal/HV paths. Relocating empty service reservations does not resolve this physical obstruction. [DES032, lines172–188](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/ce9c261a94aa2b025180f2f5c96d5e166fa01a53/docs/design/DES-032-allegro-lar-barrel.md#L172-L188), [DES033, lines110–128](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/ce9c261a94aa2b025180f2f5c96d5e166fa01a53/docs/design/DES-033-allegro-lar-endcaps.md#L110-L128)

- **Moving the endcap / extending the barrel:** useful coupled options, with clear limitations. From the recorded envelopes and \(r=z/\sinh|\eta|\), barrel full radial-depth containment ends at **1.203883**, whereas endcap full axial-depth containment begins at **1.424233**. Closing all 800 mm of warm gap still leaves the latter at **1.285638**. Making these *individual full-envelope bounds* meet would require either barrel sampling half-length **5045.705 mm**, or endcap sampling front/back **3781.044/4231.044 mm**. Preserving current closures then makes the separate vessels intersect. These are conservative geometric screening targets, **not necessary or sufficient shower-containment requirements**: combined partial barrel/endcap paths require material and response evaluation. [DES032, lines52–64](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/ce9c261a94aa2b025180f2f5c96d5e166fa01a53/docs/design/DES-032-allegro-lar-barrel.md#L52-L64), [DES033, lines45–57 and143–151](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/ce9c261a94aa2b025180f2f5c96d5e166fa01a53/docs/design/DES-033-allegro-lar-endcaps.md#L143-L151)

- **Projective overlap/common cryostat:** plausible architecture alternatives requiring new vessel, support, installation and service interfaces. They may permit sampling overlap or remove duplicate closures, but do not automatically remove service bends or access requirements. Moving the present endcap inward by more than 50 mm also intrudes into the prospective collar reservation’s overlapping radial range. HCAL envelope/field and forward beam-pipe/shielding interfaces must participate. [DES033, lines63–86](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/ce9c261a94aa2b025180f2f5c96d5e166fa01a53/docs/design/DES-033-allegro-lar-endcaps.md#L63-L86)

The 10k evidence motivates this transition study: the recorded LAr raw width is **44.18% for 999 events at \(1.2≤|\eta|<1.5\)**, versus 3.52% and 7.66% in the adjacent broad regions. It does not identify how much improvement any proposed geometry change would deliver. [10k report, lines38–49](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/ce9c261a94aa2b025180f2f5c96d5e166fa01a53/docs/validation/lar10k/README.md#L38-L49)

Next discriminating evidence: an endpoint-defined front/side/rear routing comparison, followed by combined active-depth/material maps and matched transition shower scans. Local calorimeter services should hand over to SysArch-owned external corridors; HCAL, forward-region and software representations need explicit corresponding endpoints.

| Rear outward turn | Within **w5860–6360 mm**, retain R400 mm. Allowing 20 mm independently at both axial faces requires **490 mm**, leaving only **10 mm**. A screening centreline turn starts near **w5880**, finishes radially outward near **w6280**, then continues through the rear break. Flanges, valves and supports can invalidate this allowance. |
| Exterior handoff | Route radially beyond the HCAL outline. Its 4625.9 mm outer apothem implies approximately **4716.53 mm corner radius**; **R4800 mm** is a useful provisional handoff marker, subject to magnet/yoke and installation clearance. |

The dimensional inputs and existing arithmetic are in [services.json](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/e5e1ecd68bbdcd8c3f9e6402e2089db1c8eab751/tools/lar_calorimeter/services.json#L29-L61) and [services.py](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/e5e1ecd68bbdcd8c3f9e6402e2089db1c8eab751/tools/lar_calorimeter/services.py#L46-L58).

The governing failure checks are:

- **A side port followed by an ordinary radial quarter-turn fails.** Its 470 mm one-clearance envelope exceeds the barrel/endcap corridors by **170/289 mm**. The long S-bend must occur within the redesigned neck, rather than being moved unchanged into either narrow corridor.
- **The proposed neck is occupied space.** The band contains H-rings centred at w3250/3750 and board rows near w3000/3500; the route crosses closed cold-wall/vacuum/warm-wall shells. Actual swept paths must determine which supports can be skirted and which boards or boundaries need redesign. There are only **28 spare board slots** above the 3-million-channel planning requirement, so slot removal needs a capacity check. [barrel_services.py, lines34–68](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/e5e1ecd68bbdcd8c3f9e6402e2089db1c8eab751/tools/lar_calorimeter/barrel_services.py#L34-L68), [DES032, lines132–177](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/e5e1ecd68bbdcd8c3f9e6402e2089db1c8eab751/docs/design/DES-032-allegro-lar-barrel.md#L132-L177)
- **Rear endcap connectivity is unresolved.** Signal/HV paths encounter the unported support annulus; headers, return circuits and rear penetrations also remain absent. [DES033, lines110–128](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/e5e1ecd68bbdcd8c3f9e6402e2089db1c8eab751/docs/design/DES-033-allegro-lar-endcaps.md#L110-L128)
- **An inward endcap shift does not enlarge the full radial exit window.** A 400 mm shift creates 900 mm behind the endcap, but HCAL barrel still ends at5860: unobstructed outward egress remains **5860–6360, 500 mm**. The extra room can house ports/headers inside R3130 unless the HCAL barrel or service pocket is also amended. The collar reservation separately requires redesign. [DES033, lines45–86](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/e5e1ecd68bbdcd8c3f9e6402e2089db1c8eab751/docs/design/DES-033-allegro-lar-endcaps.md#L45-L86)

A tangential/3D neck is the fallback. Turning in a tangential–axial plane can reduce radial excursion, but requires a port already oriented appropriately; rotating the drawing does not make a radial-port elbow fit.

Required handoffs: CaloTech owns cold collection, loads and neck/rear ports; SysArch owns the exterior bus, HCAL exit and common-service interfaces; magnet/field, forward-region and software owners must reconcile their boundaries. Preserve all current pipe counts initially.

Actual checks: read pinned inputs, verified all seven supplied SHA-256 hashes, recalculated bend/clearance/capacity bounds, and inspected pinned barrel-shell construction. **No files changed or runtime jobs run.** Next evidence should be one explicit utility-neck sweep plus the complete station layout and rear-port assembly; no reduced front gap is yet validated.
